c.tagline: Sherry, flamenco and dancing horses under the Andalusian sun.

taxi.fareNote: Andalusian taxis are white with a green light when free; fares are metered with fixed supplements for the airport and luggage. Uber is limited, but Cabify and Free Now operate in the area.

emergency.note: 112 is the single EU-wide emergency number connecting to police, fire and ambulance.

hood_landmark.Barrio de Santiago: Iglesia de Santiago, Jerez de la Frontera
hood_landmark.Centro Histórico: Plaza del Arenal, Jerez de la Frontera
hood_landmark.La Albarizuela: Plaza del Arroyo, Jerez de la Frontera
hood_landmark.San Mateo: Plaza de San Mateo, Jerez de la Frontera
hood_landmark.San Miguel: Iglesia de San Miguel, Jerez de la Frontera

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing rises sharply in festival crowds during the Feria and Semana Santa; keep valuables secure.

hood_desc: The walkable historic heart around Plaza del Arenal, the Alcázar, the cathedral and the great sherry bodegas of González Byass and Fundador; where first-timers stay to have the sights, tabancos and shopping at their door.

The old gypsy quarter widely called the cradle of flamenco, a maze of whitewashed lanes around the Church of Santiago that comes alive with peñas and the Festival de Jerez; steeped in atmosphere and song.
A historic parish district around the ornate Gothic-Isabelline Church of San Miguel, close to the train station and the Tabanco tapas scene; central, traditional and handy for arrivals.
A lively central pocket near Plaza del Arroyo and the cathedral packed with tabancos, tapas bars and sherry taverns; the go-to area for an evening of eating and drinking.
A quieter, elegant old-town parish around Plaza de San Mateo and the Museo Arqueológico, with churches, palaces and a relaxed local feel a few minutes' walk from the center.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout the city.

transit.hours: Urban buses run roughly 6:30 AM to 11:00 PM; the Cercanías C-1 line links Jerez, its airport, El Puerto and Cádiz through the day.
transit.note: Jerez has no metro or tram; the flat, compact old town is easily walked, with city buses and Renfe Cercanías / Media Distancia trains handling the airport and trips to Cádiz, El Puerto de Santa María and Seville.
transit.pay: Pay cash or with the Tarjeta Bus travel card on city buses; buy Renfe tickets from station machines or counters. All fares are in euros.

bus: Intercity coaches (Comes, Damas) to Cádiz, Seville and the Costa de la Luz
train: Jerez railway station (Renfe Cercanías C-1, Media Distancia and long-distance to Seville, Cádiz and Madrid)

transit.m: Renfe Cercanías C-1 train from Aeropuerto station to Jerez center (~10 min)
Bus line M-050 to the city center (~25 min)
Taxi to the city center (~12-15 min)

tip.r: Not expected; locals round up or leave small change, and about 5-10% for good restaurant service is generous.
